_README: KNOWN DIFFERENCES between runner's native C renderer and each
family's upstream jinja template. These are BUGS AWAITING FIXES,
not intentional deviations -- intentional deviations live in
This file exists so the gate is useful TODAY: it fails on NEW
drift while the pre-existing backlog stays visible and counted.
Every entry is a bug ticket. The file should only ever shrink.
Regenerate after fixing (or after deliberately changing) a case:
`status` and `note` are preserved across regeneration; the
`digest` fingerprints the (reference, runner) pair, with today's
date neutralised. If it moves, the difference changed SHAPE and
the gate says CHANGED rather than quietly accepting a second bug
`oracles` pins the sha256 of each upstream template this backlog
was recorded against. If upstream moves, the gate says so.

status_values.open: a bug nobody is working on right now
status_values.in-progress: someone is actively fixing this; see `note`

known_differences.note: Same as chatml/tool-call+result -- identical digest, same generic tool protocol substituted for Qwen's native one. Fixing one should fix both.

known_differences.note:
Qwen3 emits '<think>

</think>

' in front of a HISTORICAL assistant message's content (its template strips reasoning out of history and leaves the empty block behind). Runner emits the content bare, so a replayed conversation does not look to the model like the ones it was trained on.
Same bug as chatml-think/trailing-assistant+gen, without the generation prompt.

Tool declarations: the reference builds Qwen's native '# Tools' block with <tools>...</tools> JSON and a <tool_call> reply protocol. Runner emits its own generic '<|tool_call>call:NAME{args}<tool_call|>' protocol instead (src/server.c tools_render_for + tool_history_render_for). A protocol the model was not trained on is a real functional gap, not a formatting one.

known_differences.note: The system turn's '# Valid channels' list omits 'commentary': runner emits 'analysis, final', the reference 'analysis, commentary, final'. Harmony puts tool calls on the commentary channel, so a model told the channel is not valid is being contradicted by its own tool protocol. BEING FIXED right now by another agent -- expect these digests to move; re-run 'make template-conformance-baseline' after the fix lands.

Llama-2 restarts every user turn with BOS: the reference emits '</s><s>[INST]' at each turn boundary. Runner emits '</s>[INST]'. NOT covered by the allowlisted 'bos' deviation -- the tokenizer prepends ONE leading BOS, it does not insert one per turn. Multi-turn only.
Same as llama2/multiturn+gen (identical digest).
Same missing per-turn '<s>' as llama2/multiturn+gen, with a system block in front.
Same marker spacing as mistral/trailing-assistant+gen, over more turns.

known_differences.note: Bigger than spacing: Mistral's reference folds the system text into the LAST user turn; runner folds it into the FIRST. src/template.h says the system text is 'folded into the first user turn rather than wrapped in markers it never saw in training' -- correct in spirit, wrong turn. This one changes which tokens the model attends to, not just whitespace.

known_differences.note: Spacing: the reference emits '...sky?[/INST]', runner emits '...sky? [/INST]'. Mistral's template has no space before the closing instruction marker. Affects every mistral case.
Same as mistral/user-only+gen (identical digest).

JSON separators in the tool declaration block: the reference's |tojson emits python's default '{"type": "function"' (space after ':' and ','), runner emits compact '{"type":"function"'. Byte drift inside a block the model was trained on verbatim.

enable_thinking=false: the reference closes the block immediately ('<think>

</think>

'), runner leaves it OPEN ('<think>
'). An open think block is the opposite instruction to the one the caller asked for.
Same compact-vs-spaced JSON separators as muse/tool-call+result, inside ornith's <tools> block.

Same missing '<|endoftext|>' as phi3/user-only-nogen.
Phi-3.5 appends '<|endoftext|>' when add_generation_prompt is false; runner does not. Only affects the no-generation-prompt path, which is what prompt-continuation and scoring use.
